title: A loader report
description:
Put the milestone together: simulate what the Windows loader does when a program starts, and explain the result the way a good tool would.

A module is described by what it imports and what it exports:

```cpp
struct Module
{
    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> imports;   // (dll, function), in import-table order
    std::set<std::string> exports;                                // names this module offers
};

std::vector<std::string> loaderReport(const std::map<std::string, Module>& onDisk, const std::string& program);
```

`onDisk` holds every module that exists, keyed by file name. DLL names ignore case when you look them up; function names do not.

The report is a list of lines:

1. Work out the load order exactly like lesson 1.02's practice: depth first, a module's dependencies (the DLLs in its imports, each counted once, in the order they first appear) before the module itself, every module once. Only modules that exist are visited.
2. Before printing anything, check every module you would load, in load order, **including the program**:
   - for each of its imports, in order: the DLL must exist, and must export the function;
   - stop at the first problem and return a single line, the loader's message from lesson 1.05's practice.
3. If everything resolves, return one line `load <name>` per module in load order, then a final line `start <program>`.

If the program itself is not on disk, the report is the single line `<program> was not found.`

```
onDisk:
  game.exe   imports (audio.dll, play) (KERNEL32.dll, WriteFile)
  audio.dll  imports (kernel32.dll, CreateFileW)        exports play, stop
  kernel32.dll                                          exports WriteFile, CreateFileW

loaderReport(onDisk, "game.exe") ==
  { "load kernel32.dll", "load audio.dll", "load game.exe", "start game.exe" }
```

Use the name of each module the way it is spelled as a key in `onDisk`.
hints: First build the load order as a list of pointers to map entries, skipping DLLs that are not on disk. Then check each module's imports in that order. Only if nothing fails do you build the `load` lines.
requirements: Load order is dependencies first, each module once.
DLL names are looked up without regard to case.
The first unresolved import, in load order, stops the report with the right message.
A missing program gives `<program> was not found.`
stretch: Add a `--verbose` mode that also prints, for each module, its imports resolved to `dll!function`.
